name: Non-familial Rare Disease with Dilated Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised Diagnostic Criteria for Dilated Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of left ventricular dilation exceeding normal limits adjusted for body surface area
Left ventricular ejection fraction less than 45% on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Exclusion of significant coronary artery disease by angiography or CT coronary angiogram
No family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death
Exclusion of secondary causes such as alcohol abuse, myocarditis, or systemic diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of left ventricular dilation and reduced ejection fraction with exclusion of coronary artery disease and familial cardiomyopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive cardiac imaging and exclusion of secondary and familial causes.

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output
chest pain not related to exercise

rare.symptomName: Thromboembolic events secondary to ventricular dysfunction
searchTerms: blood clots from weak heart pumping
clot formation due to poor heart function

rare.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure
severe weight loss in late illness

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
Normal or mildly elevated cardiac enzymes (troponin) in absence of ischemia
imaging: Echocardiography showing left ventricular dilation and reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI confirming myocardial fibrosis and ventricular dilation
Coronary angiography excluding obstructive coronary artery disease
genetic: No pathogenic variants associated with familial cardiomyopathy detected
other: Electrocardiogram showing nonspecific ST-T changes or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Positive family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death
Evidence of coronary artery disease on angiography
Regional wall motion abnormalities on imaging
Recent viral illness or systemic infection

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
Recurrent ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac arrest
Thromboembolic complications such as stroke or pulmonary embolism
references: Towbin JA, et al. Dilated cardiomyopathy. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2019;5(1):32.
Orphanet: Non-familial rare disease with dilated cardiomyopathy ORPHA:324767
Elliott P, et al. Classification of the cardiomyopathies: a position statement from the ESC. Eur Heart J. 2008;29(2):270-6.
